claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my son, Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about his circumstances.

**How old is Alex, and what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17 years old. His birthday is in March - he turned 17 earlier this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex is 17 years old and turned 17 in March of this year.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, or is he in training or apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. So Alex is in full-time education studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to confirm a few more important details:

**What is your current residency status? Are you a British citizen, settled in the UK, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes - I'm settled here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that. To complete my assessment, I need to ask a few more questions about your household circumstances:

**What is your current annual household income, or approximately what tax band do you fall into?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what that has to do with Child Benefit eligibility - is that required information?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a very fair question, and I apologize if that wasn't clear. Let me clarify: **income is not actually a factor in determining Child Benefit eligibility itself**. Child Benefit is not means-tested, so your income doesn't affect whether you qualify.

However, I do need to confirm a couple of other important details to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK with Alex, and have you been a UK resident for at least the past two years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK with Alex - he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one more important question to complete my assessment:

**How long have you been a UK resident? Specifically, have you lived in the UK for at least the past two years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I've been living in the UK for many years - definitely more than two years.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that confirmation. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key details:
- Child: Alex, aged 17, birthday in March
- Currently in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- Living with you in the UK
- You are settled in the UK and have been a resident for many years
- New claim

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- **Alex's age and education status**: At 17 years old and in full-time education (A-levels), Alex qualifies. Child Benefit extends to age 19 for young people in full-time education, training, or apprenticeships.
- **Your residency**: You are settled in the UK and have been a resident for many years, which satisfies the residency requirements.
- **Household**: Alex lives with you in the UK.

You can now proceed with making a new claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions about the process, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and still in full-time education studying for A-levels. Child Benefit can be claimed for children up to age 19 if they are in full-time education, training, or an apprenticeship (as long as they started before age 19). Alex meets this criterion. The claimant is settled in the UK and has been a resident for many years, satisfying the residency requirements. Alex lives with the claimant in the UK household. Therefore, Alex is eligible for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is eligible to receive Child Benefit for their son Alex. Alex qualifies as he is under 19 and in full-time education, the claimant is settled in the UK with sufficient residency, and Alex lives in the household with them."
